1932, July
FATHER SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 46 Cont.
July 27 Promise to (come) go to (St. Bonaventure) Monastery is cure of in- curable, unmentionable Disease L. Van Steelandt (46) of Fremont O. (6 miles out on "beet wagon) contracted disease for which he doc- tored for three years - spending all his money on doctors and med- icine getting worse all the time. Three months ago he promised to come to St. Bonaventures in Detroit as soon as he could if his health were restored. At time of promise, could not turn his head. As soon as promise was made improvement was noticed. To-day he feels O.K. Thanks be to God!
July 27
Wm McKinna about 40 reported "an Orange-man" quarreled with methodest Stockwell. Had hopes of big deal going over when quarrel took place. Mck. threatened expulsion Stockwell retaliates, informing Federal authorities of McK's inditement for illegal use of mails in Califor- nia. Last night Mc lodged in jail after trying in vain to secure $5000.00 (bond) bail. A friend enrolled him and out-look has brigh- tened remarkably.
Page 47 Aug. 8 Insanity (to be cured (?) ). Nasar Russell (Arabian Ab-du ....... ) married Helen Mis'l a Belgian, in 1921. After short instructions was married not by a priest but by justice of piece. He was never bap- tized and now she is insane confined in Aloise.
Norbert Sanger - 33 - ruptured for 22 yrs enrolled yesterday. Could not go holy comunion. could not work. ...... Yesterday p.m. went out and worked - got $2. To-day comes back O.K. after holy Communion - gave 25¢ of $2. - first earned in many mo.
Oct. 8
Ruptured Apendix - Pertinitis - Pneumonia. Albert J. Cote - 68 - of Huntington Woods, Royal Oak, dying as was supposed, in Ford Hospital June 24 was enrolled in S. Mass As. that day .... Comes to monastery To-day in quite OK health. Deo Grat. - says he's good for ten years more.
Oct. 27 Margaret Byrne 57 - dying of sorosis of the liver last Thursday night as all supposed. Mrs. Law called by phone to have her enrolled - came next morning to pay for same with report that patient was almost sit- ting up. Sister Come from Chicago hoping to see her before death ar- riving at 2 a.m. To-day report patient able to feed herself.
Oct. 27 Edith Cola enrolled Oct. 22nd fearing operation for sinis, promises perpetual enrollment if things go better - enrolles To-day perpetual is O.K. - no more trouble.
